_doc: #763 THE ONE CLASSIFICATION of every shared library under ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs, and the ratchet on the one thing #763 is moving towards: an application compiles in only what it must render (gui), the thin binder client of an engine (contract), and the fleet mesh (mesh); every non-GUI capability lives in its own lib APK (engine) and is reached over IPC. A lib compiled into N apps is rebuilt N times per edit; measured over the 30 days to 2026-10-02 (commits touching the lib x apps compiling it): updater 48 x 11 = 528 ship runs, devtools 11 x 29 = 319, core 6 x 29 = 174, bottomnav 23 x 6 = 138 (GUI: those rebuilds change bytes the user sees). cloud-android-lib-classes.py (run on every push by mesh-membership-guard) fails when a lib is unclassified or classified twice, when a class contradicts what the source measurably is (an engine an app compiles in; a contract or engine that renders UI; a gui lib that renders nothing), when a mesh/contract lib outgrows its line budget, and when the backlog -- every (app, lib) edge where an app compiles in a `logic` lib -- moves off `backlog_baseline` in EITHER direction: up is a regression, down is progress that must be locked in by lowering the number in the same commit. Which apps compile which lib comes from cloud_android_lib_closure.inputs, the same answer the ship triggers and the mesh guard use.

classes.gui: Views, fragments, layouts the consuming app renders. Compiled in by definition; a change rebuilds exactly the apps that show it.
classes.contract: The thin, versioned binder client of an engine (AIDL + typed payload + client). Compiled in; must stay small and render nothing.
classes.engine: A non-GUI capability shipped as its own Cloud-Lib APK and reached over IPC. NO application may compile it in.
classes.mesh: libs:core (CONSTELLATION_DATA, the IDataBackend client) and libs:devtools (the per-process debug server, fleet provider and MESH_MEMBER receiver). In-process by necessity -- the debug server introspects its own process (Android filters logcat by uid) -- so it is allowed in every app, under a line budget so it stays minimal.
classes.pinned: Non-GUI, but bound to the consuming process by an OS boundary no IPC fixes; the reason is required.
classes.logic: Non-GUI logic still compiled into its apps: the migration backlog. Each one is a candidate engine.

ai.why: #823 the fleet's AI chat (renamed from search-page) in Compose: the page, the consent card, the assistant panel, the gateway and OpenRouter backends and the shared ai.json contract, hosted and themed by cloud-search, cloud-browser, cloud-drive and cloud-tools-small-llms. It stores nothing of its own (sessions go in the host's AiSessionStore), reads no OpenRouter key (the app hands an AiTokenSource) and ships no APK.

ai-usage.why: #1499 the read of the fleet AI usage table (c3 API GET /ai/usage): AiUsageClient (mesh first, public with the fleet bearer) and AiUsageModel (parse + card words), shared by the SuperApp Notify AI badge and Cloud SuperIntel Cost so one source feeds both. Plain JVM over org.json, renders nothing.

analytics.why: #871 engine-apk-split move 7: the contract half of the analytics sink -- the IAnalyticsSink wire, the SinkLink client, and what is per app and must survive an absent engine (the bounded per-sink queue, the consent flag, the visitor id, the site ids baked from the consuming app's build.json). The HTTP POST and the Umami/Matomo wire formats are the engine's (libs:analytics-sink). Stays dependency-free (no libs:core, no libs:databackend) because the upstream forks compile it with no shared-module graph, so the wire is its own one-method AIDL.

analytics-sink.why: #871 Cloud-Lib-Analytics-Sink: the HTTP POST of an analytics event to Umami and Matomo, in its own process; every app compiles libs:analytics (the contract) and none compiles this.

account.why: #867 the Account page (Profile, Connect, Fleet cockpit, Drift, business card), hosted by cloud-superapp and by the Cloud Account app; the host supplies its theme and routing through AccountHost.

account-ui.why: #1439 the profile pages Cloud Account and Cloud Me share: Personal Info (IDs, Pay Cards, Others, Autocomplete) and Configs (Android, Desktop, C3) in Compose; structure and sources declared once in its account-ui.json, host-only work through AccountUiHost.

apify.why: #1470 the fleet's one Apify backend choice and token store (Apify Cloud or self-hosted Cloudy Crawlee), pure Kotlin plus one encrypted prefs file, shared by reference by the apps that run Apify actors (Cloud News, Cloud Browser via libs:scraper, Media). The store is read in the calling app's process: a migration candidate once an engine serves it, so each compiling app counts as backlog.

appstore.why: The Constellation store screens, hosted by cloud-superapp and (#865) cloud-store.

auth.why: #587 sign-in and token handling shared by SuperApp and Drive, and (#867) Cloud Account: +1 backlog edge, the Connect tab IS the sign-in surface, so it runs in the app that shows it.

autofill.why: The non-secret autofill Source of Truth contract (a0_docs/eng-specs/autofill-3-tier.md): the authority, the two signature permissions, the columns, the typed rows and the pure helpers over them (derived values, candidates per field key, site-rule matching). Cloud Account serves the provider; cloud-browser and cloud-keyboard read it. Renders nothing. 520 = actual 471 + ~10%: the owner's data model (profiles with typed addresses and contacts, per-country address lines, the default-profile-per-site/TLD rule) is part of the contract every reader must agree on.

battery.why: Battery/charging policy over the adb channel, with a settings screen; SuperApp only.

cad-3dm.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's viewer lib for Rhino 3DM through rhino3dm.js: assets only (assets/cad/<lib>/loader.js and vendor/), merged into the consuming app's assets and executed in its own WebView. No code, so nothing to serve over IPC. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cad-brep.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's viewer lib for STEP/IGES through occt-import-js: assets only (assets/cad/<lib>/loader.js and vendor/), merged into the consuming app's assets and executed in its own WebView. No code, so nothing to serve over IPC. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cad-core.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's CAD model library core: pure Kotlin (ModelManifest, CadFormats, CadLibrary, ModelCache) plus the three.js viewer stage (assets/cad/viewer.html + viewer.js) the consuming app loads into its own WebView. Bound to the consuming process (its WebView, its cache dir); no IPC fixes that. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cad-dxf.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's viewer lib for DXF through dxf-parser: assets only (assets/cad/<lib>/loader.js and vendor/), merged into the consuming app's assets and executed in its own WebView. No code, so nothing to serve over IPC. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cad-ifc.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's viewer lib for IFC through web-ifc: assets only (assets/cad/<lib>/loader.js and vendor/), merged into the consuming app's assets and executed in its own WebView. No code, so nothing to serve over IPC. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cad-mesh.why: #1404 Hardtech-CAD's viewer lib for glTF/GLB, OBJ and FBX through three.js loaders: assets only (assets/cad/<lib>/loader.js and vendor/), merged into the consuming app's assets and executed in its own WebView. No code, so nothing to serve over IPC. Compile-in only; ships no lib APK.

cgc-3d.why: #1373 the CG apps' shared 3D viewer/editor: assets/cgc (three.js based runtime and vendor/) merged into the consumer's assets and run in its own WebView, plus CgcSpec, CgcConfig, AvatarEngine and OpenRouterAvatar. Bound to the consuming process's WebView and assets; renders nothing in Kotlin. Compile-in only.

ui-nav-bars.why: #1154 shared navigation + theme: the bottom nav in Compose.
#1154 shared navigation + theme: the first top row in Compose.
#1154 shared navigation + theme: the second top row in Compose.

theme-background.why: #1154 shared navigation + theme: the page background and colour roles.

ui-icons.why: #1160 shared navigation icon catalog: name to ImageVector for every nav bar.

bluetooth.why: #1221 Android Bluetooth shared by reference: the Bluetooth page (Find, Analyze, Locate, Connect, Interact, Debug, Dev; #1264) the SuperApp renders in Configs > Fleet and Cloud Calc in Measure, over one GATT stack that Cloud Browser's Web Bluetooth bridge (#1222) also drives.

nfc.why: #1264 the NFC tag analyzer shared by reference: the NfcPanel page (Scan, Write, History, Status) Cloud Calc renders in Measure > NFC, over one reader-mode controller and the NDEF parser.

usb-drive.why: #1375/#1405 USB-C drives: StorageManager volumes flattened to plain values, the per-volume SAF grant and libaums raw USB mass-storage access. The SAF grant and the USB host permission belong to the calling app's own process (the user grants them to that package), so it is compiled into Cloud Drive and Cloud Store's appstore host rather than served over IPC.

wifi.why: #1263 the Wi-Fi analyzer shared by reference: the five-tab WiFi page (Scan, Channels, Link, Tools, Log) the SuperApp renders in Configs > Setup > Network and Cloud Calc embeds, over one scan / link / tools controller.

scraper.why: #1426 Cloud Browser's Scrapers section in Compose: Site Files (cache, downloads, saved pages per site, in-app viewer) and Scrap Tools (YouTube Download via the scrappers-api container).

media-convert-audio.why: #1428 one converter: the audio track of a video remuxed on the phone (MediaExtractor/MediaMuxer, no FFmpeg). Compiled into Cloud Browser through libs:scraper (backlog 27 -> 28); a candidate engine once a second app converts media.

calc.why: #767 Cloud-Lib-Calc: libqalculate as a pinned libqalc.so behind CalcBackendService; cloud-calc binds it.

contacts.why: DeviceContacts reads the CALLER's READ_CONTACTS; runtime permissions are per package, so the engine process would read nothing (libs-backend-split).

core.why: CONSTELLATION_DATA and (#777) FleetAlerts, the fleet alerts client every app raises through. +50 lines for it: the alert API has to be in-process in every app, which is what mesh means. #783 +400 for FleetConfig + its provider, the fleet configuration contract: it reads and writes the app's OWN SharedPreferences, which no other process can open, so it is in-process in every app by necessity — the same reason as the alerts client. #796 2000 -> 1400: ProfileSyncClient (SuperApp only), ConfigSyncClient (libs:auth) and HealthStore (libs:health) left for their one consumer each -- five of the twenty core edits in the 60 days to 2026-10-03 were to those three files, each rebuilding all 32 apps. #825 1400 -> 1260: the engine wire (DataBackendClient/Service + IDataBackend) left for libs:databackend, compiled only by the engines and the six apps that bind one. 1260 -> 1190: the SuperApp pager markers (Collapsible, SuppressHorizontalSwipe, SuppressVerticalSwipe) left for the SuperApp, their one reader. 1190 -> 1080: the fleet-config manifest parsing, store classes and migration policy (FleetConfig.Manifest/exportApp/importApp) left for libs:fleetconfig-model, run for every app by the Cloud-Lib-Fleetconfig engine over IFleetConfigEngine; core keeps the provider (its own SharedPreferences read/write), the client constants and the tiny versioned engine client (FleetConfigEngine, CONTRACT_VERSION handshake).. #855 (architect, option b) 1080 -> 1100 = actual 1067 + ~3%, a ceiling, not a target: what remains is in-process by necessity. Telemetry + LogUpload: the crash handler CoreInitProvider installs in every app must run in the crashing process and get the report off it. FleetAlerts and NotificationStore: the in-app clients every app raises alerts and notifications through. FleetConfig + FleetConfigProvider + FleetConfigEngine: the app's own SharedPreferences read/write and the versioned engine client (the policy is already in Cloud-Lib-Fleetconfig). Moving more out would cost a one-app push per consumer to declare a new module, for ~15% fewer lines (rejected); a telemetry engine would lose the in-process view (rejected). 1100 -> 1195 = actual 1161 + ~3%, a ceiling: SilentChannels (+63 lines), the one place a fleet notification channel is created silent for Cloud Store (new _silent_v2 ids, no sound/vibration/light, importance <= LOW) and its old channels deleted. A channel belongs to the package that creates it, so the rule runs in-process in the posting app; FleetAlerts (here) is one of its five posters, so it cannot live in libs:updater or libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools, which depend on core. 1195 -> 1245 = actual 1208 + ~3%, a ceiling: StoreNotifyPrefs + StoreNotifyGate (Cloud Store > Configs > Notifications, the owner's per-kind/per-channel switches over the same silent Store channels). The posters that ask StoreNotifyPrefs.allows are in-process in every posting app (SilentChannels/FleetAlerts/NotificationStore are already here for the same reason: a notification belongs to the package that posts it, and the switch is stored in that package's own SharedPreferences, store_notify), and the pure matrix is held by StoreNotifyPrefsTest. Moving it to libs:appstore was rejected: libs:updater, a poster, does not compile libs:appstore, so it would have to start, for ~50 lines #1093 1245 -> 1255 = +6 lines: Telemetry sends its POST through FleetHttpSeam (libs:fleetconfig-model) first, so an app running the fleet endpoints routes it mesh first; libs:core cannot link the transport itself. #1093 1255 -> 1372 = actual 1332 + ~3%, a ceiling: the crash handler's delivery path (TelemetryRoute: the per-app /apk/<app>/logs route with the mesh origin first, TelemetryQueue: the offline queue a crash waits in until the next start, deviceMeta, and the two-leg send) +77 lines. It runs in the CRASHING process by necessity, the same reason as Telemetry itself (#855): a crash that cannot leave must be written to the app's own files dir before the process dies, so it cannot live in an engine. The moves were tried and rejected: libs:fleetconfig-model is a contract lib at 996 of its 1000-line ceiling (+98 lines would turn it red), and a new module for ~100 lines costs a one-app push per consumer (the #855 argument). 1372 -> 1500 = actual 1462 + ~2.5%, a ceiling: DataSyncBudget (the one gate for holding a dataSync foreground service, 92 lines) is in-process in every app by necessity, as the foreground service and its 6h/24h budget belong to the holding package (the updater, appstore and gallery workers all call mayHold in their own process); the rest of the growth is the same alert/notification/telemetry clients already argued above. Moving the gate out was rejected: libs:updater and libs:appstore both depend on core, and a new module for ~100 lines costs a one-app push per consumer (the #855 argument).

crash.why: #1122 the crash-safe default of every fleet app, split out of libs:core, which is AT its 1372-line budget (the budget was not raised: CrashReports left, 1531 -> 1335). Linked by libs:core (`api`) and installed from CoreInitProvider, so every app gets it with no code of its own: CrashReports (the persist-first report in files/crashes, the POST to the phone's local C3 WebServer, retry of unsunk reports, the uncaught-exception handler) and the generic crash screen (CrashActivity in its own :crash process: stack trace, Copy, Share, Retry in safe mode; Compose, with a share-sheet fallback for the apps whose build has no compose compiler). In-process by necessity, the same reason as Telemetry (#855): the handler must run in the CRASHING process and write the report to the app's own files dir before the process dies, and the screen must be in the app's own package (a crash screen of another app could not read files/crashes). It depends on nothing else in this repo, so the core -> crash edge has no cycle. 321 lines = what src/main holds (the Compose screen and its plain fallback are both counted, though one builds) + ~3%, a ceiling: 330. #1106 330 -> 460 = actual 428 + ~7%, a ceiling: SafeEncryptedPrefs (107 lines), the one place the fleet opens an EncryptedSharedPreferences file and the crash-safe default of the secret stores: a Keystore master key that does not match the surviving prefs file (shared-uid migration, restored backup) threw AEADBadTagException from Compose on the main thread (Drive #1106), so the open never throws, resets the file and key alias, and says so. It lives here because libs:core is at its budget and every app already links libs:crash (core api), so no module is added and no app build.json changes.

datamanager.why: PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS is special access granted per package in Settings; an engine would need a second grant (libs-backend-split).

disk.why: #813 the Disk Management engine reads and deletes under the CALLING app's grants: StorageStatsManager needs PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS (special access granted per package in Settings) for another app's sizes, and the shared-storage walk and every delete run under that app's all-files access. A Cloud-Lib APK would hold neither grant and read nothing; compiled into cloud-drive only, no APK of its own.

disk-scan.why: #813 libs:disk's arithmetic (walk, storage map, huge files, duplicates, clean plan), plain JVM and PIT-gated; it walks and hashes files through the calling app's all-files access, so it lives where libs:disk lives. Compiled only by libs:disk.

devtools.why: Per-process debug server, FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, DebugInitProvider. #796 1670 -> 1520: the #792 port table left this module for 1_cicd/src/data/debug-ports.json (per-root generated slices), so a new package no longer rebuilds every app; 1560 after #802 I1 (the debug API reads a request body, +47 lines, the same day).. #855 (architect, option b) 1560 -> 1600 = actual 1553 + ~3%, a ceiling: AppDebugServer + LogPipe introspect this app's own process (logcat is uid-filtered, /api/net/dns reads this app's own network); DevControlBridge is the live-activity hook ShellActivity and the DevControlServers drive; FleetPeers/FleetToken/FleetTokenProvider/FleetMemberReceiver/DebugInitProvider are the per-app mesh membership; DiagnosticsPush is called in-process by libs:updater in ~11 apps. A debug engine would not see the caller's process (rejected); declaring new modules app by app costs 15-20 pushes (rejected). #ipc 1600 -> 1860 = actual 1805 + ~3%, a ceiling: the fleet IPC layer (FleetIpc + FleetIpcWire, a0_docs/eng-specs/fleet-ipc.md) is in-process by necessity -- it is every member's IPC door (FleetTokenProvider.call -> FleetIpc.serve -> AppDebugServer.dispatch, the same route table the loopback API serves) and the typed client with its version-skew HTTP rung; the per-app loopback listener it replaces leaves in the gateway phase, which lowers this again. #ipc gateway phase 1860 -> 1640 = actual 1593 + ~3%: the per-app loopback listener (bind, accept loop, HTTP parsing, bearer check) left -- the SuperApp gateway is the one door -- and the IPC layer gained request bodies by file descriptor. #1490 1640 -> 1790: the 147-line logexport package (every app's log-export IPC door; in-process because it reads the process's own LogPipe ring), actual 1740 + ~3%

feed.why: Cloud-Lib-Feed; no app links it since the libs-backend split.

fleet-endpoints.why: #1093 THE fleet endpoint fallback (mesh `<service>.app` first, then the public URL with the fleet bearer; cached verdict; re-probe on a network change), shared by reference between Cloud Mail (core:jmap) and Cloud Account (libs:account). Non-GUI, but bound to the consuming process by an OS boundary no IPC fixes: it is the OkHttp interceptor pair on the app's OWN HTTP stack (a request cannot be rerouted from another process), it probes the mesh over the app's own network and VPN state, and the bearer must travel only on that process's own requests to the exact public origin. Plain JVM Kotlin so Mail's JVM module links it as readily as an Android library does.

fleet-endpoints-android.why: #1093 The Android halves of the fleet endpoint design, two small files: NetworkChangeWatch (the default network's transports changed, so the router re-probes the mesh) and FleetEndpointsClient (the pull of Cloud Account's published endpoint pairs over its accountdata provider). Bound to the consuming process by the OS: the connectivity callback and the provider call are the app's own, and they feed the in-process router of libs:fleet-endpoints. Renders nothing.

fleetconfig.why: #825 Cloud-Lib-Fleetconfig: the fleet-config policy every app's FleetConfigProvider (libs:core) binds over IFleetConfigEngine (plan / export / import over a dump of the app's own files). No app compiles it.

fleetconfig-model.why: #825 the typed payload of the fleet-config engine: fleet-config.json parsed into stores/classes/apps (FleetPolicy) and the policy over it, plus the dump-in/writes-out adapter the engine serves (FleetPolicyEngine). Out of libs:core, so compiled by the engine and by the SuperApp only (it plans and diffs the whole fleet with the same classes), not by 32 apps. Renders nothing. #873/#874 380 -> 780 = actual 729 + ~7%, a ceiling: the setup contract (SetupContract, SetupProvider, SetupStores, +350 lines) is the one interface every app answers and the Account vault/fleet setup drive; it reads each app's OWN stores, so it is compiled where the app runs, not in an engine. #920 780 -> 960 = actual 895 + ~7%, a ceiling: CredentialProviderStatus (is Cloud Vault the default passwords/passkeys provider: the parse of three secure settings and the settings intent per API level), read by SuperApp and Vault only; pure over Settings.Secure and Intent, renders nothing. libs:bottomnav was rejected (its Compose-port test forbids android.view) and libs:core is at its 1100 ceiling. 960 -> 1000 = actual 973 + ~3%, a ceiling: several agents' commits grew the setup contract/FleetPolicy past 960. Splitting a file inside the lib was tried and rejected: L3 sums every src/main file of the lib, so a sibling file only adds its own header/imports (994 lines after the split). 1000 -> 1090 = actual 1055 + ~3%, a ceiling: the fleet-config contract grew with the setup contract and the stores it declares (several agents' commits); it renders nothing and is compiled where the app runs. A split inside the lib was tried and rejected before (L3 sums every src/main file).

editor-core.why: #1484 the Editor's shell in Compose: the tab strip, the View | Edit toggle of a tab and the declarative file-type router (editor-types.json); persists the tabs. Compiled into Cloud-Drive, which draws it.

json-viewer.why: #1484 JSON viewer in Compose: collapsible tree, syntax colour, search, copy path and value; compiled into Cloud-Drive's Editor.

local-serve.why: #1484 loopback-only static HTTP server (127.0.0.1, random port, traversal guard) and the WebView that shows its page: the Editor's Served mode; compiled into Cloud-Drive.

log-export.why: #1490 the standalone module and test home of every app's log-export IPC provider. Its sources are NOT here: they are libs:devtools' logexport package (the provider <package>.logexport, an exported CONSTELLATION_DATA-protected ContentProvider returning the app's own recent logcat and crash ring as JSON), compiled here by srcDir so the Libs ship unit-tests them. Never on an app's classpath; devtools carries them into every app through libs:core.

media-viewer.why: #1484 view-only image, audio and video in Compose over platform APIs (BitmapFactory, MediaPlayer, VideoView); compiled into Cloud-Drive's Editor.

odf.why: #1484 odt, ods and odp view and edit in Compose (an odt through libs:wysiwyg, an ods as a table, an odp as slides); the package I/O is java.util.zip plus the platform XML DOM. Compiled into Cloud-Drive's Editor.

pdf.why: #1484 PDF view (platform PdfRenderer) and edit (PdfBox-Android: annotate, form fill, page delete, reorder, rotate) in Compose; compiled into Cloud-Drive's Editor.

wysiwyg.why: #1484 THE shared WYSIWYG engine: block model, Markdown and HTML codecs, edit ops, Compose editor and viewer; compiled into Cloud-Drive's Editor and Cloud-Notes' native Markdown view (ownership decided later).

firewall.why: A VpnService runs under the VPN consent of the app that requested it; moving it moves the consent and drops the tunnel.

gh.why: #705 GhBackendService execs libgh.so in Cloud-Lib-Gh; Drive binds it.

git-ui.why: #1408 Cloud Drive's git manager UI (repo table header, metadata table; the sheet, menus and solver follow), rendered by cloud-drive with its look lent through LocalGitUiKit.

git-repos.why: #1408 Cloud Drive's git repo model (scan, sync history and schedule, Auto Commit core, auto checks, stale-pack cleaner), plain JVM and PIT-gated; it reads repositories under the app's own grants, compiled into cloud-drive only.

git-core.why: #1408 THE in-process git engine: JGit (clone, fetch, pull --rebase, stash, push, conflicts, upstream) on any storage root with typed errors, the models and the JSON verb surface. Plain JVM, PIT-gated. It reads and writes repositories under the calling app's own All files access, so it is compiled into cloud-drive (through libs:git-sync) and ships no APK of its own. Replaces the retired Cloud-Lib-Git-Sync-Engine.

git-sync.why: The GitSync screen (GitSyncScreen: repositories, changes, log, branches, remotes, settings) hosted by cloud-drive, the repository registry, the credential store (keystore-backed, the app's), the auth-chain walker and the GitEngine client. #1408 the engine runs in-process: libs:git-core (api) answers every verb in cloud-drive's own process through InProcessGitTransport; the separate engine APK is retired.

gix.why: Cloud-Lib-Gix (binary engine); no app compiles it.

kde-connect.why: KDE Connect protocol client, SuperApp only.

databackend.why: #825 the generic engine wire (IDataBackend.aidl + DataBackendService + DataBackendClient), out of libs:core: compiled by the eight engines that extend it and the six apps that bind one, so a wire edit no longer rebuilds all 32 apps. Package unchanged.

decisions.why: #772 the thin client of a REMOTE engine, OpenRouter's Decisions API: one POST and its answers read back as probabilities. Compiled by Cloud Calc (jev/) and by the image engine's OpenRouter route; renders nothing.

decisions-core.why: #881 the PIT harness of the decisions engine's logic: it compiles the engine's own core package as plain JVM, runs its suite and mutation-tests it (gate 80). The logic lives in libs:decisions-engine's directory so the publish gate (own dir only, #870) republishes the engine when it changes; nothing here ships and no app may compile it (L2).

decisions-engine.why: #881 Cloud-Lib-Decisions-Engine: the one place the fleet asks the Jev decision model anything, holding the OpenRouter token in its own process, the per-use declarations, budget, consent, cache and journal; every app compiles libs:decisions-link (the contract) and none compiles this.

decisions-link.why: #881 the contract half of the decisions engine: the IDecisionsEngine wire (no credential in it), the DecisionsLink client (handshake before any bind, bound for one call) and the typed Verdict an app reads. Dependency-free like libs:analytics so the upstream forks can compile it. #882/#883 320 -> 430 = actual 381 + ~12%, a ceiling: Advice (the shared call-site plumbing of every Jev use: a deadline that never waits on the main thread, a bounded memo of suggestions, and the pending-outcome file that lets a standing suggestion count as accepted after a week). It lives here once because it wraps DecisionsLink.report/outcome and every consuming app needs the same behaviour; one copy per call site (15 apps) was the alternative.

ml-l-image.why: engine-apk-split move 6: IImageScanEngine wire + typed payload + client. #772 raised 460 -> 620 for contract 2: the uniform Recognition result both routes answer in, the request built from recognition.json and the per-app route/model choice -- the parse and the prefs every consumer needs, no recognition logic (that is the engine's). #799 raised 620 -> 790 for RecognitionRoutes: the ONE route switch both apps share for image and sound (Model (Jev) first, the offline/no-token/error fallback, the per-type last-route record the debug routes report) -- a rule both apps must apply identically, so it lives in the contract they compile, not in either app.

ml-l-image-mlkit.why: Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Image-Mlkit (ZXing + ML Kit OCR; #772 recognition; #798 live detection with a full-label classifier).

ml-l-sound.why: #798 ISoundEngine wire + the SoundEngine client + sound.json (THE sound-identification declaration) + the per-app route; the answer is libs:ml-l-image's Recognition. Cloud Calc and Cloud Camera compile it; YAMNet and TFLite are the engine's. #799 raised 300 -> 360 for SoundRouting: the Model route's request, its context line and the spectrogram it attaches, built where the samples are (the image engine that carries the request to OpenRouter never sees audio).

ml-l-sound-yamnet.why: #798 Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet: YAMNet (521 AudioSet classes) on LiteRT behind SoundBackendService; Cloud Calc and Cloud Camera bind it.

headless-browser.why: #1498 The fleet's headless browser for agents (off-screen WebView sessions on a VirtualDisplay, headless-api v1 over a signature ContentProvider and a loopback listener). A non-GUI engine of Cloud Browser, which owns the WebView, compiled into it; stops when idle, no keep-alive. backlog_baseline 30 -> 31 for the one new edge (cloud-browser, headless-browser).

ocr.why: #1507 OCR result toolkit (pure Kotlin: table detection, Markdown, sidecar JSON, naming, sha256 skip rule); reads no pixels, the engine stays the Ml-L-Image-Mlkit APK. Compiled into Cloud Drive for the Screenshot OCR agent. backlog_baseline 29 -> 30 for the one new edge (cloud-drive, ocr).

ml-l-image-ocr.why: #1418 (renamed from libs:ml-ocr to libs:ml-l-image-ocr) OCR (ML Kit Text Recognition with the bundled script models, and the OpenRouter vision transport), compiled into Cloud Writer for its Load image / Take picture boxes. On the migration backlog: the candidate engine is an IOcr binder served by a Cloud-Lib APK. backlog_baseline 27 -> 28 for the one new edge (cloud-writer, ml-l-image-ocr); #1428 (media-convert-audio via scraper) took 27 -> 28 concurrently, so the merged baseline is 29.

model-catalogue.why: The fleet's model catalogue (selection, OpenRouter pricing, section filter) and its Compose page, moved out of Cloud Search so Cloud Code's Chat shows the same catalogue (A0 Code only). Cloud Search compiles it as a module and hosts the page; Cloud Code, a Cordova WebView with no Compose, compiles its logic package and assets by reference (build-extras.gradle) and draws the table in DOM from CatalogueJson.

mounts.why: The Mounts screen (MountsScreen: the mount list, the add dialog, the browser with download, upload and commands) hosted by cloud-drive. #871 engine-apk-split move 12: the ftp / ftps / sftp / ssh / webdav clients and the connections they hold left for libs:mounts-engine; what stays is the screen, the models, the mount list, the credential store (keystore-backed, the app's) and the thin client (the IMountsEngine wire, MountLink handshake-and-bind, EngineFs as the RemoteFs the browser uses). It leaves the backlog (28 -> 27) because the logic compiled in is now the engine.

mounts-engine.why: #871 Cloud-Lib-Mounts-Engine: sshj, commons-net and OkHttp and the authenticated connections they hold between calls (by handle, closed when idle), in their own process, with the credentials the caller sends for the call that opens a connection and nothing kept; cloud-drive compiles libs:mounts (the contract) and not this. Holds its own All-files grant (Store > Access > Android Perms) for downloads and uploads in the shared store.

perms.why: #1274 the permission contract AND the per-app Permissions page: the catalogue asset every grant is declared in, the live status reader, the exact-settings opener, the auto-request batch planner, the ADB block generator, PermsNeeds, PermsLink, the shell/fleet grant rules (PermsShell, PermsGrant) and PermsActivity, the Compose page every app without a PermsHost page renders (permissions are per package, so each app hosts its own). Gui since #1285: compiled into each app that embeds a lib using it, and it draws.

net.why: Typed INetBackend + Tunnel state/config types; the engine is libs:net-wg.

net-wg.why: Cloud-Lib-Net-Wg (libwg-go.so moved out of every app).

ops.why: The Dagu page (DaguFragment: DAG list, Run buttons, bearer login) hosted by cloud-superapp and C3. #871 engine-apk-split move 8: its HTTPS calls to Dagu and the parse of its two payload shapes left for libs:ops-engine; what stays is the page, DaguPrefs' encrypted server URL and bearer, and the thin client (the IOpsEngine wire, OpsLink's handshake-and-bind, the typed DaguClient). Classified gui, not contract: a contract draws nothing, and this one draws the page. An absent engine shows the sentence that says what to install.

ops-engine.why: #871 Cloud-Lib-Ops-Engine: the HTTPS calls to Dagu (list the DAGs, start one), in their own process and only to the fleet's declared Dagu host; the SuperApp and C3 compile libs:ops (the contract) and neither compiles this.

rclone.why: The Rsync screen (RcloneScreen: remotes, jobs with live progress, browse) hosted by cloud-drive. #871 engine-apk-split move 10: the pinned static rclone binary and the process that execs it left for libs:rclone-engine; what stays is the screen, the rclone.conf and job files (the app's, private), the parsers and the thin client (the IRcloneEngine wire, RcloneLink handshake-and-bind, RcloneRunner). It leaves the backlog (30 -> 29) because the logic compiled in is now the engine.

rclone-engine.why: #871 Cloud-Lib-Rclone-Engine: the pinned static rclone, exec'd in its own uid with the rclone.conf the caller sends for one call and nothing kept; cloud-drive compiles libs:rclone (the contract) and not this. Holds its own All-files grant (Store > Access > Android Perms) for jobs on the shared store.

search.why: The search ENGINE, UI-free since the SuperApp's one search (each app draws its own results): matching, the per-scope sections, the scope model and per-entry defaults, the colon-command rule, and the SearchSource interface an app fills from its OWN process (its LauncherApps view, its section index, its PackageManager's Settings screens). It ranks that in-process index on every keystroke, so an IPC hop per letter would buy nothing: plain logic compiled where its data lives, as disk-scan is. A static lib (#870), not an engine APK.

shared-store.why: cloud-shared-store's store-access layer: the ICloudExec wire (same AIDL as termux's CloudExecService), the runtime mode decision (DIRECT when the shared uid cld.termux.shared is in effect, else EXEC through CLOUD_EXEC), the store/guest path rules and the legacy-path migration rule. Reads ac_cloud-termux/build.json::shared_store; renders nothing. Compiled by Cloud Drive, and (SharedUidMigration) by libs:appstore's hosts SuperApp, Cloud Store and Cloud Account for the generated ICloudExec client that starts the old terminal's home backup — one AIDL, no hand-written binder call. 260 -> 285 = actual 277 + ~3%, a ceiling: the store-access layer grew with the shared-uid and legacy-path migration rules; it renders nothing and is the one contract its hosts compile.

shell-broker.why: #1510 THE one owner of the privileged shell: wraps the embedded ADB / Shizuku channel of libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools behind a signature-guarded provider and bound service, the per-caller command allowlist (default deny), the audit log, a timeout on every call and a concurrency cap. Bound to the SuperApp by an OS boundary no IPC fixes: the channel is the SuperApp's own adb pairing and its Shizuku-compatible provider, and the caller identity is read from the binder uid inside this process. Compiled by the SuperApp only; every other app links libs:shell-client.

shell-client.why: #1510 The thin client of the shell broker: ShellClient.exec/stream/status/arm over the SuperApp's signature-guarded provider and ShellResult (Ok / NeedsArm / Denied / Failed). Renders nothing, links no other project (not libs:core, not the shizuku lib), declares no service and no receiver: an app that needs a shell links this instead of its own adb channel. Plain Android + org.json. #1512 240 -> 300 = actual 283 + ~6%, a ceiling: the stdin door (execStdin, the stdin wire keys, the size and timeout clamps, ShellWire + ShellClient, 107 lines) is the growth the first ceiling reserved room for; the terminal-only rish relay (189 lines, used by 2 of the 6 apps) left for libs:shell-rish instead of raising the budget to 472.

shell-rish.why: #1512 `rish` for the two terminals (Cloud Terminal, Cloud Nix terminal), split out of libs:shell-client: RishRelay (the loopback relay a proot `rish` calls, token per process) and ShellRish (writes the launcher + rish.env), both answering through libs:shell-client's ShellClient, the thin client of the shell broker. Renders nothing, declares no component; its one project dependency is libs:shell-client. The engine stays the broker (libs:shell-broker, SuperApp).

shizuku-adb-debug-tools.why: The embedded adb client (pairing, shell door): SuperApp's privileged plane, and the dialog-free install channel of SuperApp and (#865) Cloud Store. +1 backlog edge for cloud-store: an install session belongs to the app that opens it, so the store cannot reach it over IPC. (#867) Cloud Account +1: it links libs:appstore for the Fleet tab's inventory, which brings the channel with it. 2026-10-06 +2 (27 -> 29): the terminals (cloud-termux, cloud-nix-on-droid) now compile it as the fallback privileged channel behind SuperApp's own provider (615c8dfd0) -- the adb pairing door must run in the app that owns the pty, so the edge is by necessity, like the installer's. 2026-10-13 +1 (29 -> 30): Cloud Drive compiles it for Manage ▸ Apps: running state and PSS of OTHER apps come only from a shell (ps, dumpsys meminfo); it is a client of the SuperApp bridge first, the channel ladder is the lib's and a shell reply cannot be handed across an IPC hop without a second privileged service.

sound-tags.why: #798 the sound engine's own arithmetic (WAV decoding, resampling, windows, averaging, the model's label list), plain JVM and PIT-tested; compiled only into Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet, so no app may compile it (L2).

sysdns.why: #741 SystemDnsBridge is a loopback resolver the terminal's own proot guest talks to, inside that app's process; ResolverProxy likewise for the gh/rclone/gix binaries.

text-tools.why: ITextTools binder contract + client; the AIDL method order is the wire format.

translate.why: Translation engines + TranslateBarView (#667: a language engine carrying a host-embedded bar), keyboard only.

ui-kit.why: #773 the shared Compose kit: theme over the launcher palette, tiles, rows, dialogs, KitComposeFragment.

updater.why: Self-update and the store's install machinery (PackageInstaller sessions, APK cache, GHCR client), compiled into 11 apps -- the largest fan-out by measured cost. Moving it moves the install-permission identity. #865 cloud-store is the 12th app (+1 backlog edge): it IS the installer, so the engine must run in its process. #867 cloud-account is the 13th (+1): Updater.start is every app's self-update and the Fleet tab reads the install engine.

voice.why: Voice engines + model manager + VoiceBarView, keyboard only.

watchdog.why: ICloudExec binder contract + bridge, c3-watchdog only.

web-core.why: #1371 the fleet's one embedded web view: CloudWeb (factory, profiles, desktop mode), the client bases, the GPU probe.
